newsitem.title: ITALY: 1950s fire finally dies out in Italian court.
newsitem.headline: 1950s fire finally dies out in Italian court.

text.p: A retired forestry worker was ordered to pay damages for a fire nearly 40 years ago at the end of a 17-year-long Italian court case on Wednesday.
Pasquale Salis, 75, was told by the court in the Mediterranean island of Sardinia to pay five million lire ($3,200) plus interest and costs to the island's regional authorities.
The blaze, fanned by strong winds, broke out in August 1957 as Salis was burning a fire break on public land and spread to private property.
Regional authorities took Salis to court in 1979 after damages were awarded against them in a civil suit brought by the property owners.
Salis's case was not untypical in Italy, where the judicial system is painstakingly slow.
